Professor: Xu Han  
Course: CS211  
Department: Computer Science
University: George Mason University
Source: Rate My Professors
Document Type: Student Reviews

Review:
Grade: A  
Rating: 5/5  
Difficulty: 2/5  
Tags: Caring, Lecture Heavy, Accessible Outside Class  

Student Feedback:

Han's CS211 lectures are somewhat monotonous but concise and focused on material needed for the midterm and final exams. Compared to other computer science courses, students describe the exams as straightforward. Programming assignments are generally manageable except for the final assignment. The reading workload is heavy at the beginning of the semester but becomes lighter later.

Review:
Grade: A-  
Rating: 3/5  
Difficulty: 3/5   
Tags: Get Ready to Read, Lots of Homework, Lecture Heavy  

Student Feedback:

Students describe Professor Han's teaching style as dry and monotonous. The course includes a significant amount of reading during the first few weeks. Some students report changing deadlines, unclear programming assignment grading criteria, lengthy lecture slides, and complex lab exercises. However, exams are generally viewed as easier than the assignments.

Review:
Grade: C-  
Rating: 1/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Programming Assignments Difficult  

Student Feedback:

Some students report that programming assignments are extremely difficult and that lectures are unengaging. They also note that the assignments and exams do not closely reflect the coding examples demonstrated during lectures.

Review:
Grade: A-  
Rating: 3/5  
Difficulty: 4/5   
Tags: Get Ready to Read, Lots of Homework, Caring  

Student Feedback:

Students indicate that Professor Han appears to care about the course and students' success, but lectures are often described as boring. Early course readings require a substantial time commitment. Some students recommend independent study because they found the pacing and progression of lectures unusual.

Review:
Grade: A-  
Rating: 3/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Lots of Homework, Heavy Reading, Monotone Lectures  

Student Feedback:

Students generally describe Professor Han as pleasant but note that lectures can be difficult to follow due to a monotone speaking style. Even students with prior Java experience report difficulty keeping up with the volume of graded reading assignments. The course workload is commonly described as heavy.

Rating: 4.2/5

Student Feedback:

Students frequently describe Professor Zhong as caring, patient, and supportive, particularly for students with little or no prior programming experience. Many reviews mention that she provides numerous examples during lectures and is willing to answer questions both during and outside of class.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5

Student Feedback:

The most common criticism concerns lecture delivery. Many students describe lectures as dry, repetitive, or boring. Several reviews note that lecture material often overlaps heavily with textbook readings and online learning materials.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Lots of Homework, Heavy Workload, Time Management Required  

Student Feedback:

Students consistently report a substantial workload throughout the semester. Projects, labs, homework, and online readings require significant time commitments. Students strongly recommend starting projects early and avoiding procrastination.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Project Heavy, Time Consuming, Hands-On Learning  

Student Feedback:

Projects are the most frequently discussed aspect of the course. Students report that projects require many hours to complete, with final projects being the most difficult. However, they are also seen as effective for reinforcing programming concepts. Success depends heavily on starting early.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Clear Grading Criteria, Extra Credit, Fair Exams  

Student Feedback:

Students generally describe grading as fair and transparent. Exams are considered manageable with preparation, and practice questions often align closely with assessments. Extra credit opportunities are also frequently mentioned.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Beginner Friendly, Office Hours Helpful, Steep Learning Curve  

Student Feedback:

For beginners, the course can feel overwhelming at first due to a steep learning curve. Office hours are highly recommended. Students with prior programming experience find the course easier but still time-consuming.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Caring, Helpful, Supportive Instructor  

Frequently mentioned strengths include a caring instructor, helpful feedback, accessibility outside class, and strong support for beginners. Students often describe Professor Zhong as one of the best CS112 instructors.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Heavy Workload, Boring Lectures, Fast Difficulty Increase  

Common concerns include boring lectures, heavy workload, and a noticeable increase in difficulty after the first few weeks. Some students also mention communication issues and time-consuming assignments.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5  
Difficulty: 3/5  
Tags: Time Management, Consistency Required, Project Success Strategy  

Student Feedback:

Students consistently emphasize success strategies such as starting projects early, completing readings regularly, attending office hours, and practicing coding outside of class. Time management is repeatedly highlighted as essential.

Review:
Rating: 4.2/5

Tags: Positive Overall, Recommended, Intro CS Course  

Student Feedback:

Overall sentiment is strongly positive. Despite workload and lecture criticism, students recommend the course for beginners due to strong support, fairness, and structured introduction to programming concepts.
